title: Implement Dynamic Heartbeat Configuration for Ingestion Service
description: The PulseSphere platform is a distributed system of microservices. The operations team requires more control over service behavior without needing to recompile and redeploy code. Currently, the `ingestion_service` uses a hardcoded interval for its main processing loop, which acts as a heartbeat and processing trigger. This task involves modifying the service to read this interval from its configuration file, allowing for dynamic tuning in production environments.

project_spec.name: PulseSphere: Real-Time Social Pulse Streaming Platform
project_spec.description:
PulseSphere is a high-throughput, event-driven data-streaming platform written in C that captures, validates, transforms, and disseminates live "social pulses" (likes, comments, shares, follows, and reaction emojis) from multiple social networks, community forums, and in-house engagement widgets. Each pulse is modeled as an immutable event and published into a unified event fabric, enabling downstream microservices to continuously compute community sentiment, trending topics, and influence graphs in near real-time.

Designed around a microservice-oriented Data Lake and Pipeline Pattern, PulseSphere ingests millions of heterogeneous social events per second, performs schema-on-read validation, parallel enrichment (geo-tagging, language detection, toxicity scoring), and streams curated data into analytical sinks for data scientists while simultaneously driving interactive dashboards for moderators. Fault-tolerant batch windows reconcile late and out-of-order events, and Strategy Pattern plug-ins allow rapid experimentation with alternative enrichment, quality-check, and visualization strategies without redeploying the entire system.
dependencies: librdkafka (C client for Apache Kafka) – Event streaming backbone
libuv – High-performance event loop & async I/O
Apache Arrow C Library – In-memory columnar representation for batch and stream interoperability
Flatbuffers or Google Protobuf-C – Compact, schema-versioned message serialization
libpq / PostgreSQL – Metadata & configuration store (Data Lake catalog)
Redis Streams (hiredis) – Low-latency pub/sub for hot paths (e.g., moderator alert channels)
OpenSSL – TLS encryption for cross-datacenter event transport
Prometheus C Client & Grafana – Telemetry, health metrics, and data visualization endpoints
Parquet-C and libhdfs – Batch off-loads to HDFS-backed Data Lake
OpenMP / Intel TBB – Parallel processing of transformation stages
cJSON / RapidJSON C wrappers – Lightweight JSON generation for UI APIs
libarchive – Compressed batch file handling in cold-storage workflows
